Q: How do reflection and multi-agent debate differ from independently verified evidence?
A: Reflection asks a model to critique or revise an answer; debate asks multiple roles or agents to propose and challenge alternatives. These may expose mistakes but remain correlated when they share a model, prompt assumptions or source material. Agreement is not the same as an independent measurement or an authorized decision. Use verifiable intermediate outputs, independent sources where available and a bounded arbitration policy. Prefer a simpler deterministic workflow when roles add tokens without improving measured outcomes.
Why: Three specialist agents agree that a policy permits an action because all read the same incomplete excerpt. A fourth debate round cannot supply the missing exclusion; checking the complete governing source can.
Risk: More agent roles can amplify one unsupported assumption and diffuse accountability.
Trade: Add roles for distinct capabilities or evidence, not simulated consensus alone.
Try: Compare debate with a single-agent baseline on a shared-source failure case.
